name: Lair Derg

attributes.attribute: fairy queen of southeastern County Limerick
could take the form of an unbeatable horse

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lair Derg was a name or title that meant red mare. It was used of the goddess Aine, the fairy queen of southeastern County Limerick. Red is generally an Otherworld color in Celtic belief. Aine could take the form of an unbeatable horse called Lair Derg. Her feast stood on midsummer night or on Lughnasa, the first of August. At that time people waved straw torches over animals and drove them up the slopes of Knockainy to ask her protection. She was also called Aine Chlair. Among her many lovers were the sea god Manannan mac Lir and the human earl of Desmond.

okr.objective: Record Lair Derg as the red mare title of the goddess Aine of County Limerick.
